speakers.name: Caroline Pascal
speakers.bio: Caroline Pascal is a robotics engineer at Hugging Face, working on the LeRobot team. She’s become the team’s unofficial Swiss army knife, jumping across the library while focusing on expanding data modalities and models to make AI for robotics more accessible. She is also involved in the development and promotion of Reachy Mini, where she mainly focuses on the robot’s acoustic design and chips in on core media functionalities—basically making sure robots not only work, but sound good doing it.

speakers.name: Chao Jia
speakers.bio: Chao Jia, Vice President of Technology at ModelBest and Co-founder of the OpenBMB open-source community. He is primarily responsible for organizing the R&D and open-source management of the MiniCPM series of on-device models. Dubbed the "ModelBest's Little Steel Cannon" the MiniCPM family—which includes the MiniCPM large language model and he MiniCPM-o omni-modal model—has earned widespread acclaim in the global AI community for its high efficiency, low cost, and ability to "punch above its weight." To date, these projects have amassed over 30,000 stars on GitHub and exceeded 24 million downloads worldwide, establishing themselves as benchmark works in the field of on-device AI.

speakers.name: Charbel Dandjinou
speakers.bio: Charbel is the founder and CTO of Reflexion Robotics, a Paris-based startup building A OS  - a safety runtime for embodied AI. Previously AI Research Engineer and MLOps Tech Lead at EXXACT Robotics. He also founded IROKO and the Deep Takka research lab, focused on making AI accessible and inclusive.

speakers.name: Christian Maitre
speakers.bio:
A digital transformation and innovation expert with extensive international leadership experiences in Telecom
President & Founder – Caspera-Lab, Founder of Caspera-Lab, a premier global advisory firm specializing in guiding the telecom companies to (re) build, review, (re)start their sustainable digital transformation journeys with AI, genAI and Agentic AI.
Former CIO deputy for Digital Transformation – Orange Group, 10 years as Group CIO driving digital transformation worldwide  (21 opcos),
TM Forum partner / ambassador, Recognized contributor to TM Forum innovation programs, founder of the autonomous networks concepts, leader on digital Maturity evaluation project
Foreign Trade Advisor of France (CNCCEF), Chair of the Digital-IA-Tech Expert Group at CNCCEF a french governmental association.

speakers.name: Dong Xin
speakers.bio: 2008–2017: Technical Leader at Microsoft, working on the Microsoft Azure enterprise cloud and Dynamics 365 platform R&D. 2017–present: Technical Expert and Product Director at Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., working on the R&D of core infrastructure software including toolchains, programming languages, and IDEs. During his time at Huawei, he has served successively as Chief Technical Expert and Project Manager, working on Huawei’s mobile AI R&D tools, the company-wide AI R&D platform, the Huawei Ascend AI chip toolchain, and the HarmonyOS toolchain, among other initiatives. Since 2021, he has been responsible for the R&D of Huawei’s programming language and IDE infrastructure software, serving as Program Director. He leads the core technology R&D of proprietary and independently-controlled programming languages and IDE development tools, and has made significant contributions to the technical planning, productization, and industry adoption of domestically-developed application programming languages.
speakers.roleOrg: Program Director, Central Software Institute, Huawei

speakers.name: Gaotian (Vector) Wang
speakers.bio: Gaotian (Vector) Wang is a Computer Science PhD student at Rice University. He is the creator of XLeRobot, a fully open-source, low-cost ($660) dual-arm mobile robot platform that has gained 4.8k+ GitHub stars and a global community of 6,000+ builders since its release in May 2025. XLeRobot is built on the Hugging Face LeRobot ecosystem and has been adopted by researchers, educators, and hobbyists worldwide.

speakers.name: Guillaume Blaquiere
speakers.bio:
Guillaume is a Google Developer Expert on Cloud Platform since 2019 and works at Carrefour as Group Data Architect. 

Initially Java developer, and despite positions of responsibilities, he has always kept his wish to create, develop, discover and test new solutions, especially in the Cloud, the AI & genAI. He notably contributed to Python and Go open source project and libraries (Google SDK, Airflow, ADK). 

Innovation addict and Google Cloud 3x certified, writer and speaker in his free time, he’s fascinated by the serverless and genAI solution and all the "usual" problems that they solve.

speakers.name: Jeremy Laville
speakers.bio: Mechanical engineer, with strong passion for robotic. Worked for Aldebaran on Pepper robot, and more recently on Reachy 2 for Pollen Robotics. I also designed Amazing Hand open source project.

speakers.name: Jiaming Liu
speakers.bio: Jiaming Liu is a Ph.D. student at the School of Computer Science, Peking University. His research focuses on robotic manipulation and embodied foundation models. He has published 20 papers as first author or co-first author at top-tier international conferences, including CVPR, ICLR, and RSS (CCF-A or CAAI-A venues). His work has received over 3000 citations on Google Scholar. In terms of honors and awards, Jiaming Liu has received the 2025 ByteDance Scholarship (awarded to only 20 recipients), the National Scholarship, and the Peking University Presidential Scholarship. In international competitions, he won the championship in the ICCV 2023 Continual Generalization Learning Challenge, the championship in the Robust Multi-Task Learning Challenge, and third place in the CVPR 2023 Autonomous Driving Occupancy Prediction Challenge. He has also been invited as a keynote speaker and panelist at GOSIM 2024, the 2nd China Embodied Intelligence Conference, and the China Generative AI Conference. At the project level, he has successfully secured funding from the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Young Scientists Fund) and the China Association for Science and Technology (Young Elite Scientists Sponsorship Program).

speakers.name: Jigyasa Grover (co-speaker Rishabh Misra)
speakers.bio:
12-time award-winning AI lead and 'Sculpting Data For ML' author Jigyasa Grover drives rider personalization innovation at Uber after transforming Twitter/X, Facebook/Meta, Faire, and Bordo AI with large-scale ML systems. Handpicked by Google for their I/O keynote, she serves on Google's Developer Advisory Board while advising social search engine Diem and other Silicon Valley startups. 

As a LinkedIn Learning instructor, Jigyasa educates thousands of professionals worldwide on cutting-edge AI-powered applications and agentic AI systems, solidifying her status as a thought leader in artificial intelligence education. As a Google Developer Expert, Women Techmaker Ambassador, and World Economic Forum Global Shaper, Jigyasa has also been featured in Forbes, Business Insider, VentureBeat, and International Business Times, and has elevated panels with Harvard University, Preston-Werner Ventures, Norwegian Business School, Humanitarian Frontier in AI, Women in Data, and more to her name. 

The UC San Diego alumna has secured funding from the Canadian and Norwegian governments, the Linux Foundation, and multiple tech giants, enabling work that transcends geographical boundaries. With 200+ media features and contributions to open source recognized by Apache and Python Software Foundations, she mentors next-generation talent while shaping AI's future through advisory roles at Bezoku AI, Las Positas College, and various AI forums.

speakers.name: Jinwei Gu
speakers.bio: Dr. Jinwei Gu is currently a Principal Research Scientist at NVIDIA and an Adjunct Associate Professor at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, working on generative AI, world models, and the general fields of computer vision, computer graphics, and machine learning.  He received his Ph.D. in Computer Science from Columbia University in 2010, and B.S. and M.S. from Tsinghua University in 2002 and 2005, respectively. At NVIDIA, Dr. Gu is one of tech leads in cosmos model development – a family of multimodality world foundation models, with a focus on enabling real-world applications in robotics, autonomous driving, and generative AI. Prior to joining NVIDIA, he worked at SenseBrain as a R&D Executive Director, focusing on mobile computational photography with novel image sensors and imaging systems. He has published extensively in top-tier conferences and journals, and serves as an Associate Editor for IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI) and IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging (TCI) (2018-2023), an Area Chair for CVPR, NeurIPS, ICCV, ICCP, and ECCV, and organizing chairs for several workshops (MIPI, RichMediaGAI).  He is an IEEE senior member since 2018. His research work has been successfully transferred to many products such as NVIDIA-Cosmos, NVIDIA-CoPilot SDK, NVIDIA-DriveIX SDK, as well as Super Resolution, Super Night, Portrait Restoration, RGBW solution which are widely used in many flagship mobile phones.

speakers.name: Luke Lu
speakers.bio: Luke is a student at the University of Texas at Austin and the founder of Correx, an open-source robotic task verification and safety compliance layer. His journey in robotics began as a competitor, rising through the ranks of competitive robotics to claim a world championship title. That experience ignited a drive to mentor aspiring engineers and contribute to the open-source robotics community. Today, Luke channels that same competitive energy into founding technology ventures at the intersection of AI and robotics, believing that the best ideas should be accessible to everyone willing to build them.

speakers.name: Marcin Zubrzycki
speakers.bio: I'm a SWE @ StrongDM (now part of Delinea), I'm currently studying Algorithmic Computer Science @ WrocTech - Love my country and my girlfriend.

speakers.name: Markus Tavenrath
speakers.bio:
Markus Tavenrath studied computer science with a focus on computer graphics at RWTH Aachen University. This academic background provided a solid foundation for his career in the technology industry.

In 2008, Markus joined NVIDIA, where he began working on real-time ray tracing on GPUs. Over the years, he has contributed to performance optimization for ray tracing, scene graphs, OpenGL, WebGL, Vulkan, and AI. His work has played a role in advancing these technologies.

Markus is also a co-founder of the Vulkan-Hpp project, which has been beneficial to the Vulkan community. His efforts have helped improve the use and implementation of Vulkan.

Recently, Markus was elected as the Chair of the ML Council at Khronos. In this role, he helps coordinate and support AI and machine learning initiatives within the Khronos group. His election to this position reflects his expertise and leadership qualities.

Markus Tavenrath is a dedicated professional whose contributions have positively impacted the technological landscape at NVIDIA and beyond.

speakers.name: Merel Theisen
speakers.bio: I am a Principal Software Engineer at QuantumBlack, where I am currently the tech lead of Kedro, an open-source project part of the Linux Foundation. I have over ten years of experience in the software industry, with most of my career focused on backend product engineering. I am passionate about building products that solve real user problems, and I care deeply about creating robust, well-tested software that follows good engineering principles. I am also a strong advocate for open-source software, and I find working with the community to be both inspiring and energising.

speakers.name: Minakokojima
speakers.bio: I'm the Head of Developer Relations at Kimi, where I've also held positions in post-training and infrastructure. Prior to joining Kimi, I worked as an algorithm engineer at Google. I won several gold medals at ACM ICPC regional contests during college.
speakers.roleOrg: Head of Developer Relations, Moonshot AI (Kimi)

speakers.name: Nouamane Tazi
speakers.bio: Nouamane Tazi is a Machine Learning Research Engineer at Hugging Face, specializing in training large language models. He is a co-author of SmolLM3 and The Ultra Scale Playbook, and his research spans NLP, deep learning, and scalable AI infrastructure.

speakers.name: Priyanka Jain
speakers.bio: Building non-invasive brain computer interfaces.

speakers.name: Qingyue (Annie) Wang
speakers.bio: Annie Wang is a is a Software Engineer, Developer Advocate, and Internal Career Coach at Google where she helps developers build with AI. With 7 years of software engineering experience and 500+ career coaching hours at Google, she brings both technical depth and a talent for making complex concepts accessible. Annie specializes in Multi-Agent Systems, Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK), and Agent Evaluation, and has delivered keynotes at DevFest NYC, Boston, and Beijing. She is known for her "learn by doing" approach, helping engineers move from theory to building production-ready AI applications.

speakers.name: Ran Shemtov
speakers.bio: Ran is a web developer with over a decade of experience building products for the web. Since 2023, he has been deeply involved in the emerging world of AI-powered applications, helping companies design and bring AI agents into production. At CopilotKit, Ran works closely with teams building real-world AI experiences, guiding them through the challenges of turning LLM prototypes into systems that serve real users.

speakers.name: Rik Arends
speakers.bio: With 20+ years’ experience as a C/C++, JavaScript and more recently Rust developer, I've always been excited by using computation for visuals and audio. For this to work you need performance, and a smooth workflow enabled by the right tooling. After having everything I wanted with C except stable code I moved to JavaScript and web technologies. However, this never got to the point of being able to make fast applications that use modern CPU and GPU power. Now with Rust we have a new chance. I've been an entrepreneur my entire life building VJ software in the 00's, then web UI technology and web IDEs with Cloud9, and am now reimagining the developer workflow in Rust with Makepad. And lately how to leverage AI to write Rust and UI code.

speakers.name: Shiwei Liu
speakers.bio: Shiwei Liu is a group leader at Max Planck Institute for Intelligent System and a PI at ELLIS Institute Tubingen. He was a Royal Society Newton International Fellow at the University of Oxford. He previously served as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Texas at Austin. He obtained his Ph.D. with Cum Laude from Eindhoven University of Technology in 2022. Dr. Liu has received two Rising Star Awards from KAUST and the Conference on Parsimony and Learning (CPAL). His Ph.D. thesis received the 2023 Best Dissertation Runner-up from Informatics Europe. He has a broad interests of life-cycle of large foundation models.
speakers.org: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
speakers.roleOrg: Group Leader & PI, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems

speakers.name: Sylvain Corlay
speakers.bio:
Sylvain Corlay is the founder and president of QuantStack, a company specializing in open-source software for scientific computing.

As an open-source developer, Sylvain is highly active in the free scientific computing ecosystem, particularly in the Jupyter project, as well as in the conda-forge and xtensor projects. In 2018, he was honored, along with other Jupyter leadership members, with the ACM Software System Award.

Beyond QuantStack, Sylvain is deeply involved in the community. He served on the board of directors of the NumFOCUS Foundation from 2018 to 2024, organized JupyterCon 2023 in Paris, and has coordinated the PyData community in Paris since 2017, acting as the organizer of the meetup group and the PyData conference in 2024 and 2025.

speakers.name: Sébastien Crozet
speakers.bio: Sébastien Crozet has been in love with the Rust programming language since its earliest days. He is the creator and maintainer of popular open-source libraries, including nalgebra and Rapier, for the Rust ecosystem that specialize in linear algebra, geometry, and physics. He is the founder of Dimforge where he focuses on contributing to the future of cross-platform scientific computing and AI.

speakers.name: Tim Head
speakers.bio: I am a scikit-learn and cuML maintainer. I work at NVIDIA

speakers.name: Virgile Batto
speakers.bio: Robot Architect. I optimize,design, and control legged robot

speakers.name: Weiyu (Ervin) Xie
speakers.bio: Weiyu Xie is a fifth-year Ph.D. student in the Institute for High Performance Computing, Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University. His research interests include computer systems, large language model (LLM) inference, graph computing, and databases.

speakers.name: Wenzhe Cai
speakers.bio: An Embodied AI researcher, working on building an open-sourced embodied navigation foundation models.

speakers.name: Xinyuan Tong
speakers.bio: SGLang Maintainer

speakers.name: Xuan-Son Nguyen
speakers.bio: I'm software engineer at Hugging Face, core maintainer of llama.cpp

speakers.name: Yonghui Wu
speakers.bio: Dr. Yonghui Wu, associate professor at Fudan University, visiting scholar at Stony Brook University, and, the chair of the ICPC Asia Training Committee. He won three medals in ACM ICPC World Finals for Fudan University. His book series “Collegiate Programming Contests and Education” has been published in simplified and traditional Chinese and English: the former by respective publishers of mainland China and Taiwan, and the latter, the first book’s translation, by CRC Press. Since 2013, he has been giving lectures not only in China, but also in other countries.

speakers.name: Yuhao Yang
speakers.bio: SGLang Developer

speakers.name: Yuxuan Zhang
speakers.bio: Technology Evangelist at ZhipuAI.

speakers.name: Zhipeng Huang
speakers.bio: Zhipeng Huang currently serve as Director of AI Open Source for Huawei. Zhipeng is now the Board chairperson of LFAI&Data Foundation, TAC Chair of Open Model Initiative, executive member of CCF Open Source Development Committee, co-lead of the Kubernetes Policy WG, project lead of CNCF Security SIG, founder of the OpenStack Cyborg project, and co-founder of OpenStack Public Cloud WG. Zhipeng used to give Keynote presentations at OpenStack Summit, KubeCon and RISC-V Workshop
